mismo writes a types file listing every route's pattern and its params. `Link`, `useNav`, `Redirect` and `useParams` are typed from it, so a link to a route that doesn't exist, or without its params, fails the typecheck.

```ts title="src/routes.gen.ts"
// Generated by mismo from the shared routes folder. Do not edit.
import type {} from "@mismo/core";

declare module "@mismo/core" {
  interface Routes {
    "/": Record<never, never>;
    "/orgs/[id]": { id: string };
    "/sign-in": Record<never, never>;
  }
}
```

Keep it somewhere TypeScript can see it, such as `src`, and there's nothing to import.

## Setting them up

Each app already gets its own types file, from the `types` path in its build setup. It has the shared routes plus its platform's own, for the app's own screens.

The shared package's screens need one too. List it in the config, and write it with `mismo types`:

```ts title="packages/app/routes.config.ts"
export default defineRoutes({
  source: "./routes",
  input: expo.input(),
  validFor: [next, expo],
  types: { shared: "./src/routes.gen.ts" },
});
```

```json title="packages/app/package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "typecheck": "mismo types --config routes.config.ts && tsc"
  }
}
```

That's all most projects need.

## Routes on one platform

A route with only a `.web` or `.native` file exists on one platform. The shared types leave it out: a shared screen runs on both platforms, so it can't link there.

```tsx title="routes/orgs/[id].tsx"
<Link to="/">All organizations</Link>

{/* @ts-expect-error: /billing is web only, and this screen is shared. */}
<Link to="/billing">Billing</Link>
```

The same link in the web app's own code typechecks, since the web app's types include its platform's routes.

## If you use platform files

If the shared package has `.web` or `.native` files that link to platform-only routes, those files need their platform's types, and the plain files must not see them. List a file per platform:

```ts title="packages/app/routes.config.ts"
types: {
  shared: "./src/routes.gen.ts",
  web: "./src/routes.web.gen.ts",
  native: "./src/routes.native.gen.ts",
},
```

Then check each platform's files on their own, since one TypeScript program would see every types file and allow any route. Use a tsconfig per platform, tied together with project references:

```json title="packages/app/tsconfig.shared.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "react-jsx", "moduleResolution": "Bundler" },
  // The plain files, with the routes every platform has.
  "include": ["routes", "src"],
  "exclude": ["**/*.native.*", "**/*.ios.*", "**/*.android.*", "**/*.web.*", "src/routes.*.gen.ts"]
}
```

```json title="packages/app/tsconfig.web.json"
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.shared.json",
  // The web files, with the shared routes plus the web ones.
  "include": ["routes/**/*.web.*", "src/**/*.web.*", "src/routes.web.gen.ts"],
  "exclude": []
}
```

`tsconfig.native.json` is the same with `native`. The root `tsconfig.json` references all three, so `tsc -b` and editors use the right one for each file:

```json title="packages/app/tsconfig.json"
{
  "files": [],
  "references": [
    { "path": "./tsconfig.shared.json" },
    { "path": "./tsconfig.native.json" },
    { "path": "./tsconfig.web.json" }
  ]
}
```

The typecheck script then runs `tsc -b` instead of `tsc`.

## Pattern syntax

Patterns match how you [defined the routes](/docs/routes-folder#other-ways-to-define-routes): `/orgs/[id]` in an Expo Router folder, `/orgs/:id` in a React Router config. Groups aren't part of a pattern: `(app)/home.tsx` is `/home`.
